memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: glaucoma, insomnia, and gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease.
Patient reports mild blurring of vision, trouble initiating sleep, and occasional post‑prandial heartburn. Examination shows normal visual acuity, relaxed eyelids, no conjunctival injection; abdomen soft, no tenderness. He is a never‑smoker, pack‑years 0. Intra‑ocular pressure will be checked, and spirometry is not required as there is no asthma/COPD. Plan: start topical glaucoma therapy, melatonin and trazodone for sleep, PPI for reflux, and arrange baseline labs.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Intra‑ocular pressure: right eye 18 mmHg (10‑21), left eye 19 mmHg (10‑21).
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L (0.4‑4.5).
Haemoglobin: 13.8 g/dL (13.0‑17.0).
H. pylori stool antigen: negative (reference: negative).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: stable glaucoma, insomnia improved, GERD controlled.
Patient says vision unchanged, sleeps 5‑6 hours with melatonin/trazodone, heartburn rare after using pantoprazole. Eyes: IOP 18/19 mmHg, no conjunctival redness. Abdomen benign. No medication side‑effects noted. He remains a never‑smoker. Continue current meds, consider reducing trazodone if daytime drowsiness appears.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Optic disc assessment and visual field test (Humphrey 24‑2).
Discs: cup‑to‑disc ratio 0.6 right, 0.5 left, within normal limits for age. Visual fields: full, no defects. No glaucomatous progression detected.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up pulmonology appointment booked for 2025-09-20 at 10:30 am.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: glaucoma stable, insomnia well controlled, GERD in remission.
Patient reports good sleep (6‑7 hrs), no daytime sedation, no heartburn for 4 weeks. IOP 17/18 mmHg. Visual fields unchanged. No adverse effects. He remains a never‑smoker. Continue current regimen; consider tapering trazodone further if sleep remains solid.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: glaucoma stable, insomnia worsened after trazodone taper, GERD asymptomatic.
Patient reports difficulty staying asleep, waking after 4‑5 hrs, feeling fatigued. No heartburn. IOP 17/18 mmHg. He denies new ocular symptoms. He remains a never‑smoker. Plan: discontinue trazodone due to residual daytime grogginess, increase melatonin to 5 mg HS, add sleep hygiene counselling.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Upper GI endoscopy performed for alarm symptom of unexplained weight loss (not present) – performed due to persistent mild epigastric discomfort despite PPI.
Findings: mild gastritis, no ulcer, no Barrett’s epithelium. H. pylori rapid test negative. Biopsy negative for malignancy.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Gastroenterology, Bangalore Medical Centre, for opinion on refractory gastritis and to rule out microscopic colitis. Include recent endoscopy report and PPI trial details.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Gastroenterology review: gastritis likely NSAID‑related (patient denies NSAIDs). Recommend continue PPI, consider low‑dose amitriptyline for visceral hypersensitivity, repeat H. pylori stool antigen in 3 months. No further endoscopic intervention needed.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: "Since stopping trazodone and increasing melatonin, I’m sleeping about 6 hours a night and feel more refreshed in the morning. No heartburn issues." – message via clinic app.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: glaucoma stable, insomnia improved on melatonin alone, GERD controlled.
Patient reports sleep 6‑6.5 hrs, no nocturnal awakenings, feeling rested. IOP 16/17 mmHg. Visual fields unchanged. No medication side‑effects. He remains a never‑smoker. Continue melatonin 5 mg HS, timolol and latanoprost, pantoprazole as needed.
